messages:
maya: quick question — my embeddings batch helper is failing on a customer dataset. half the batches return vectors of length 1536 and some return 768 after a model variant rolled. any tips for safe pagination + batching behavior?
kevin: which model are you calling? sounds like a model switch (or a fallback to a smaller embedding model) returning a different dim.
maya: we call the hosted /embeddings endpoint via our client helper. config is model: "open-embed-1536" but the rollout may have a canary that returns a different variant. we batch with page size 512 and then slice results into pages.
aaron: common pitfalls: 1) not validating embedding dimensionality per-response, 2) merging batches without checking lengths, 3) reusing memory buffers assuming fixed dim.
kevin: devex suggestion: always assert embedding.length == expectedDim for each item, and if mismatch, log model returned + request id, then either requeue that item for single-item retry or fail the batch fast depending on SLA.
sophia: small snippet we use in the python SDK to be defensive:
```python
EXPECTED_DIM = 1536
for item, emb in zip(request_items, resp["data"]):
    if len(emb["embedding"]) != EXPECTED_DIM:
        logger.warning(f"embedding dim mismatch: expected={EXPECTED_DIM} got={len(emb['embedding'])} model={resp.get('model')} id={item.id}")
        handle_dim_mismatch(item)
```
maya: nice. question: what should handle_dim_mismatch do? re-embed single item? switch model?
kevin: we do a tiered strategy in the helper: 
- if it's a one-off, requeue single-item call to the same model (with jitter/backoff)
- if >X% of batch fails with same model, mark model as degraded in cache and fallback to pinned stable model for next N requests
- emit metric embedding.dim_mismatch with model tag
aaron: also add a guard when paginating: sometimes pages come back with partial results if the server times out. detect length(request_items) != len(resp["data"]) and retry the page (idempotent) or fetch missing ids.
sophia: re pagination: use stable cursor-based pagination from API when available. avoid assuming ids are contiguous indexes.
maya: streaming quirk: when using streaming embeddings (we do chunked responses), our parser sometimes concatenates chunks and loses alignment — resulting in index shifts so dims map to wrong input. any parsing tips?
kevin: always attach a per-item request_id and echo it through the request metadata so the response can be re-associated. if streaming, include a header like x-request-shard or item-id in the request payload.
sophia: PR #421 addresses some of this: it adds per-item uuids, per-response dim checks, and a small state machine to mark models degraded. maya can you try that branch? @maya :eyes:
maya: will try. also curious about retry/backoff values — we default to exponential with max 10s. good?
aaron: depends on your latency requirements. single item retry backoff 100ms * 2^n with jitter, max 1s for interactive, 10s for async batch jobs.
maya: thanks. last Q: how to surface this to customers? we want helpful errors not raw API dims.
sophia: map to SDK error EmbeddingDimensionMismatch with fields: expected, got, model_name, request_id, and guidance message: "re-run with pinned model or contact support". send telemetry with sample hashed input for debugging.
maya: great. i'll run PR #421 branch against the failing dataset and post logs. pinging @kevin for review when drafts ready.
ci-bot: build passed for branch feature/embeddings-defensive (ci: 2026-03-17T12:30:00Z) :white_check_mark:
kevin: thanks! happy to review, put a draft PR link and I'll take a look tomorrow morning. :+1:
